title: A Rivergate for the Provision
premise: Freya Zhou, a storm chaser drowning in debt to the Optimists—a cheerful, ruthless lending syndicate—takes one last contract: map the drowned coastline before monsoon season. When an unprecedented low tide exposes a sea cave that local legend says grants passage to anyone desperate enough, Freya finds a dying cartographer inside clutching a chart of a river that flows backward. Pursued by both the Optimists' collectors and a government warden sworn to seal the source forever, Freya follows the river upstream with Mara Ilesanmi, the cartographer's estranged daughter who wants justice more than treasure. At the forbidden source—a spring that preserves perfect memory—Freya must choose between selling its location to clear his debt and destroying the map to protect it, while Mara chooses him over her vengeance. The monsoon makes landfall as they flood the source themselves, erasing the legend but keeping each other; Freya returns to face the Optimists with nothing but testimony, and discovers the wilderness remembered them kindly after all.
about_author: B. M. Villalobos is the pen name of a former hydrologist who spent six years surveying river systems across three continents before turning to fiction. They write adventure novels in which landscapes are characters, debts are weather, and every map is a confession.

chapters.title: The Debt Collector Smiles
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. In a flooded coastal bar, the Optimists' collector Pell offers Freya a final contract: survey the drowned shelf at Cape Verren before monsoon, or lose his boat and his fingers. The beat is dread disguised as charm—Freya signs because optimism, he learns, is the most dangerous currency.

chapters.title: Storm Chaser's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Preparing the boat, Freya tallies what he owes against what he owns and comes up short in everything but skill. Flashbacks to the storm that killed his old crew establish his guilt. The emotional beat is quiet self-loathing sharpened into resolve.

chapters.title: Cape Verren, Low Water
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Arriving at the cape, Freya meets hostile locals who warn him about the cave that 'charges admission.' An impossible tide begins to fall—the lowest in a century. The beat is unease: the land itself seems to be making him an offer.

chapters.title: What the Tide Gives Back
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The retreating sea reveals the cave mouth, ribbed like a throat. Against every instinct, Freya enters with lamp and line. Inside he finds a skeleton, a brass instrument, and a waterproof chart of a river flowing inland from the sea. Beat: awe curdling into greed.

chapters.title: The Dying Cartographer
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The skeleton isn't dead yet. Old Tomás Ilesanmi, trapped by the returning tide, gives Freya the chart and a warning—'the source remembers you back'—before dying. Freya barely escapes the rising water. Beat: horror and the first weight of obligation.

chapters.title: Mara
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. In the port town of Salt Hollow, Mara Ilesanmi has spent nine years petitioning the Survey Office to search for her missing father. She recognizes Freya's salvage gear being sold. The beat is cold fury meeting opportunity.

chapters.title: Accusation at the Harbor
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Mara confronts Freya with theft; he shows her the chart and Tomás's last words instead of running. Warden Cass Okonjo observes the exchange, noting the illegal chart. Beat: two griefs colliding into an uneasy alliance.

chapters.title: The Warden's Oath
chapters.summary: Cass's POV. Cass reports the chart to her superiors and receives orders she finds monstrous: recover the document, then seal the source permanently with charges, burying the legend and any proof of Tomás's discovery. Beat: duty beginning to taste like ash.

chapters.title: Terms of Partnership
chapters.summary: Freya and Mara's POVs. They negotiate: Mara gets the truth about her father and justice against whoever left him to die; Freya gets the source's location to sell to the Optimists. Neither trusts the other. Beat: transactional love's first, awkward spark.

chapters.title: Upstream
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. They launch up the coastal river on Freya's patched boat, following the backward-flowing current that defies every law Freya knows. First sign of pursuit: Pell's launch on the horizon. Beat: exhilaration—the wilderness finally feels honest.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Toll
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. At a derelict ferry crossing, an ancient woman demands payment 'in memory, not coin,' taking one of Mara's childhood recollections as passage. Mara can no longer recall her mother's face. Beat: the theme made flesh—memory has a price.

chapters.title: Pell Catches Up
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Pell boards them at night, all smiles, offering to double Freya's debt if he surrenders the chart—or forgive it entirely if he delivers the source alive and mapped. Freya stalls. Beat: the trap tightening with terrible courtesy.

chapters.title: Rapids of the Forgotten
chapters.summary: Both POVs. A flash flood forces them through rapids; Freya nearly drowns reliving his crew's deaths in vivid detail the river seems to feed him. Mara saves him. Beat: intimacy forged in near-death, trust outpacing the contract.

chapters.title: The Survey Office File
chapters.summary: Cass's POV. Cass reads Tomás's sealed file and discovers the Survey Office abandoned him deliberately—he had found the source years ago and refused to weaponize it. Her orders were written by the same man who signed his death warrant. Beat: loyalty cracking.

chapters.title: Villagers of the Middle Reach
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. A river village where elders remember everything perfectly—no funerals, no forgetting—shows them the cost of the source: a community unable to heal, preserving every grievance for generations. Beat: wonder inverted into warning.

chapters.title: Freya's Confession
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. By firelight, Freya admits the storm that killed his crew was his call—he chased data over safety. Mara admits she'd have traded anything, even this journey, to have her father back. Beat: mutual absolution neither asked for nor expected.

chapters.title: Okonjo on the Water
chapters.summary: Cass's POV. Cass intercepts them alone, off the record, and warns them the demolition convoy is three days behind her—and that Pell has bought influence inside the Survey Office. She hasn't decided whose side she's on. Beat: the law revealing its own fault lines.

chapters.title: The Chart's Second Layer
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Under lamplight, Freya discovers Tomás hid annotations beneath the ink: coordinates, yes, but also a mechanism—a way to flood and seal the source from within. Tomás never intended to sell it. He meant to bury it. Beat: the father's true legacy revealed.

chapters.title: Pell's Ultimatum
chapters.summary: Pell's POV (first appearance). The Optimists' ledger balances people like weather fronts. Pell orders collectors to take Mara as leverage, reasoning that grief makes men punctual. Beat: villainy rendered as bookkeeping—chillingly reasonable.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Gorge
chapters.summary: Both POVs. Collectors seize Mara; Freya trades the chart for her freedom, then reveals he memorized and altered key coordinates. They escape down a side channel. Beat: love openly declared through sacrifice, though neither says the word.

chapters.title: Monsoon Watch
chapters.summary: Cass's POV. Satellite imagery confirms the monsoon will make landfall in four days, early. Cass must choose: follow orders and seal the source with everyone inside, or go rogue. She burns her orders. Beat: duty transformed into choice.

chapters.title: The Stair Cut in Stone
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The river narrows into a canyon where steps carved millennia ago climb beside falls that flow upward. Local carvings depict travelers trading their worst memories for passage. Beat: myth becoming geography, terror becoming pilgrimage.

chapters.title: Mara's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. In a carved antechamber, the walls show visions: her father's final days, his refusal to sell, his hope that someone would finish his work. Mara grieves properly for the first time in nine years. Beat: catharsis—justice reframed as truth-telling.

chapters.title: The Source
chapters.summary: Both POVs. They reach it: a spring-lit cavern where the water holds images—every person who ever drank from it, living their memories in the current. Freya sees his lost crew, whole and forgiving. Beat: overwhelming temptation to stay forever.

chapters.title: What Freya Sees
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. The source shows Freya his crew's last moments—not blame, but trust. He understands they forgave him long ago and that he's been paying interest on a debt already cleared. Beat: grace, undeserved and undeniable.

chapters.title: What Mara Sees
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The source offers Mara her mother's face back and her father alive. She reaches for the water—and stops, understanding that a memory kept here is a life not lived. Beat: renunciation as the hardest form of love.

chapters.title: Pell Arrives Early
chapters.summary: Pell's POV. Having tortured the route out of a captured villager, Pell enters the source chamber with collectors and survey equipment, planning to bottle and sell the water. He drinks deeply. Beat: the optimist meets compound interest.

chapters.title: Drowning in Yesterday
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The source overwhelms Pell—he relives every cruelty he committed as its victim, trapped in recursive memory. His collectors flee. Freya and Mara drag him out rather than let him die there. Beat: mercy toward the unforgivable.

chapters.title: Cass Makes Landfall
chapters.summary: Cass's POV. Cass arrives with the demolition charges just as the monsoon's first bands hit the coast. She finds Pell catatonic, Freya standing guard over the spring. She raises her sidearm—and lowers it. Beat: the law choosing conscience over command.

chapters.title: The Argument at the Spring
chapters.summary: All four POVs interwoven. Freya argues to seal it; Cass argues the world deserves to know; Mara argues some knowledge should stay wild. The debate is interrupted by the gorge beginning to flood. Beat: ideological climax compressed into survival stakes.

chapters.title: Tomás's Mechanism
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Following the hidden annotations, Freya and Mara find the sluice gates Tomás prepared decades ago. Triggering them will flood the cavern and redirect the spring deep underground—forever. Beat: the dead father's hand guiding the living.

chapters.title: Thirty Seconds of Forever
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Before triggering the flood, each takes one moment at the water. Freya says goodbye to his crew; Mara lets her parents go; Cass releases her career; even broken Pell whispers something. Beat: collective farewell, sacred and swift.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: All POVs. The monsoon hits as the gates open. The source collapses inward, the river reverses to its natural course, and the four fight through rising black water as the legend drowns. Beat: apocalyptic set piece—nature reclaiming its secret.

chapters.title: Afterwater
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. They surface downstream, battered, alive, the chart destroyed. Cass declares them officially lost persons—free, in the eyes of the law, to disappear. Beat: exhaustion edged with improbable lightness.

chapters.title: Settling with the Optimists
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya walks into Pell's office carrying only testimony: the source is gone, the chart destroyed, and Mara's affidavit documents the syndicate's crimes. With Pell institutionalized and records seized by Cass's allies, the debt dies uncollected. Beat: justice outside the law, paid in full.

chapters.title: The Village Remembers Differently
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Returning downstream, they find the perfect-memory village changed—the spring's shift loosened the elders' grip on old grievances; the first funeral in generations is held. Mara reads her father's name aloud. Beat: mourning finally possible, healing finally begun.

chapters.title: Cass's Report
chapters.summary: Cass's POV. Cass files a report stating the source never existed—protecting the region from exploiters—and resigns her commission. She keeps one thing: a vial of ordinary river water, a private joke against certainty. Beat: the bureaucrat becoming a keeper of small truths.

chapters.title: A Rivergate for the Provision
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Freya and Mara rebuild his boat at Cape Verren, where the cave has vanished under the returned tide. He asks her, not the wilderness, whether she'll stay. She answers by handing him the tiller. Beat: love chosen freely, duty redefined as devotion.

chapters.title: The Storm They Chase Together
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Months later, they chase a storm not for data or debt but for the joy of it, mapping coastlines for communities, not syndicates. In the last line, Freya realizes the wilderness forgot nothing—it simply chose, like them, what to carry forward. Beat: resolution, warm and earned.
